synopsis: New South Wales guidance addresses mining vehicle-interaction controls, favoring site design, segregation and procedures, with collision systems at Levels 7–9 as backup; the glossary states that NSW does not mandate automatic braking [f2786, f3624, f15525]. Regulator evidence reported no meaningful year-on-year reduction in vehicle interactions in 2023 and 30 underground coal LHD/personnel-transport collisions in the 12 months to mid-2025; bulky loads sometimes obstructed LHD operators’ views [f3004, f3196, f11447]. The 2023 regulator paper also reported that NSW mining had not yet implemented proximity/detection technology reliably able to distinguish hazardous from spurious conditions, supporting the corpus’s concern about unresolved false alarms [f3112, f15540, f15551]. Although several chapters describe 0.60 m/s² as the in-service minimum off-road deceleration, the glossary clarifies that the thresholds are proposals, not adopted rules: service/secondary brakes require 0.60/0.30 m/s² in service and 0.75/0.40 m/s² for type testing, with grade and mass corrections [f141, f5889, f13946]. NSW formulas use net deceleration on grade and assume no skidding; in the 100 t truck example, a 20% design grade and 9% test grade yield a 1.04 m/s² grade correction and 1.79 m/s² required test deceleration, underscoring why definitions and test conditions must be reconciled across standards [f13640, f6295, f5902, f5901, f6614].
